newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS launches mutual funds for China, Europe.
newsitem.headline: UBS launches mutual funds for China, Europe.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) is launching two mutual funds for the emerging markets of China, Taiwan and Hong Kong and for European firms likely to benefit from monetary union.
Nicholas Fliess, a senior official with Intrag, the company which manages UBS funds, said the two open-ended funds, both based in Luxembourg, would be launched by January 29.
"We'll be launching more mutual funds this year. Client demand is growing all the time," he said.
UBS has more than 80 mutual funds, which give investors an opportunity to tap riskier markets with better returns, with portfolios currently worth a total of 60 billion Swiss francs.

The first fund, China Dragon, will invest mainly in equities in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong but also in other markets in the region with close links to these countries, Fliess said. It will be managed by UBS Asset Management East Asia in Singapore.

The second fund, Eurowinners, will focus on European Union markets and companies that will benefit from the introduction of the single European currency, the euro, and European integration, he added. It will be managed by UBS in London.
Both funds will be marketed in Switzerland and globally and target investors willing to take risks.
